column3: Close to the Hebrew; NASB refers to Dagon as “his”/“him” where the Hebrew pronoun can mean “it.”
“Only Dagon remained on it” is rendered “only the trunk of Dagon was left to him”; “trunk” is supplied.
Close to the Hebrew; “devastated” is rendered “ravaged.”
“His hand is hard” is rendered “His hand is severe,” and “Dagon our God” as “Dagon our god.”
Close to the Hebrew; “rulers” is rendered “lords.”
“Panic” is rendered “confusion,” and NASB adds “so that” before the tumors.
“To kill me and my people” is rendered with plurals, “to kill us and our people.”
“Panic of death” is rendered “a deadly confusion”; “me and my people” becomes “us and our people.”
